newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end sharply higher on bonds, banks.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end sharply higher on bonds, banks.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended sharply higher on Friday, energized by a bond rally and soaring bank shares in the wake of tame U.S. inflation figures.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 51.66 points to close at 5243.27, five points shy of the index's record high of 5248.37.
Trading was heavy with 89.4 million shares exchanging hands for a total value of C$1.4 billion ($1 billion).
In New York, the Dow Jones average jumped 67 points to a new closing high of 5839.
"It's nice to see the bears getting gored here," said Josef Schachter, a market strategist with Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.
"All this fear that the Fed was going to tighten and the economy was running rampant has been put to bed by PPI and CPI," he said.
U.S. consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in August, compared to economists' expectations for a 0.2 percent increase. On Thursday, U.S. producer prices also calmed inflation concerns.
Toronto stocks received a boost from Canadian bonds which rallied along with U.S. treasuries on the American data. Canada's 8.00 percent bond rallied 1.10 to 102.50 to yield 7.775 percent.
* Bank stocks led the rally in interest-rate sensitive groups.
Canada's five biggest banks hit new highs, including Royal Bank of Canada which rose 1 to 37.20, a 52-week peak.
Analysts said bank stocks are also attracting investors following Royal Bank's C$1.1 billion ($800 million) share buyback announced on Thursday.
Among other top gainers, Bank of Montreal climbed 0.70 to 34.60 after reaching a high of 34.65.
* Newbridge Networks Corp. rallied 3.60 to 93.40 on 842,000 shares after news of a proposed two-for-one stock split.
* Higher bullion prices powered gold stocks ahead. TVX Gold Inc. improved 0.10 to 10.40 on 1.5 million shares.
